value: What three conditions make installing an anti-misfueling device preventive maintenance under item (28)?
reason: Item (28) joins its three conditions with 'and', so all three must be met; the old front and back ('Any two of') implied two were enough. 14 CFR 43 Appendix A(c)(28).

value: The device is in the aircraft type certificate data; the manufacturer gave FAA-approved installation instructions; the existing tank filler opening is not disassembled.
reason: All three conditions are required: 'provided the specific device has been made a part of the aircraft type certificiate data ..., the aircraft manufacturer has provided FAA-approved instructions ..., and installation does not involve the disassembly of the existing tank filler opening' (Appendix A(c)(28)).

value: Item 3, when no approved data exists: the FAA grants a field approval by completing and signing it.
reason: The front asks which item, but the old back never named it. Handbook p. 2-39 (PDF p. 88): 'Item 3 is used when there is no existing approved data ... grant a field approval, shown by completing and signing this area.'

value: An approved MEL is for one specific aircraft and needs a letter of authorisation; a master list is developed for a kind of aircraft.
reason: The old back ('A master list may exist or not for a type') reads twice. 91.213(a)(1)-(2): an MEL 'exists for that aircraft' with a letter of authorization; 91.213(d)(1): aircraft kinds 'for which a Master Minimum Equipment List has been developed'.

value: The difference matters because 91.213(d) lets some kinds of aircraft fly without an approved MEL, depending on whether a master list has been developed for them.
reason: Says why the distinction matters, in line with 91.213(d)(1)(i)-(ii).

value: On a piston single with no MEL, the landing light fails before a day flight. It is not equipment required for day visual-flight certification, not on any equipment list, not required by 91.205, and no AD applies. What must happen before take-off?
reason: 91.213(d)(2) has four conditions; the old stem omitted (d)(2)(i), 'Part of the VFR-day type certification instruments and equipment', and the kinds of operations equipment list in (d)(2)(ii), so the answer did not follow from the facts given.

value: Flight manuals are usually listed in the aircraft TCDS, so the manual is a required item for the aircraft to be airworthy.
reason: The old back ('Because they are...') had no clear referent for 'they' and left out the step to airworthiness. Handbook p. 2-33 (PDF p. 82): 'These manuals are usually listed in the aircraft TCDS, and therefore are a required item for the aircraft to be considered airworthy.'

value:
A) Yes, with an airframe rating
B) Yes, if he holds an inspection authorisation
C) Yes, if supervised by the aircraft owner
D) No: the list is a suitably rated repair station, a continuous-programme holder, or the aircraft manufacturer that installed the transponder
reason: 91.413(c)(3) names 'The manufacturer of the aircraft on which the transponder to be tested is installed, if the transponder was installed by that manufacturer'; 'the installing manufacturer' could be read as the transponder maker.

value: C counts 12 months to the same date instead of to the end of the month. B treats March 2025 as the first of the 12 months. D ends the period at the calendar year, which the rule does not do.
reason: The old reason for B ('counts to a date') did not describe 28 February 2026, which is the end of a month. 91.409(a): 'within the preceding 12 calendar months'.

value: The owner or operator petitions the local FAA Flight Standards office for approval, so the aircraft can be inspected in stages instead of losing it for one long inspection.
reason: 'Airworthy at all times' is not in the cited handbook passage (it is in 91.409(d)). Handbook p. 2-21 (PDF p. 70): 'The owner/operator may petition the local FSDO for approval of a progressive inspection program.'

value: Two copies are needed because a signed copy goes to the aircraft owner and a copy is forwarded to the FAA Aircraft Registration Branch.
reason: Appendix B(a)(2)-(3) requires a signed copy for the owner but only 'a copy' for the FAA; the old wording implied both were signed copies.
